title: Dereferencing
summary: The * operator follows a pointer to the object at its address, to read it or to write it. Two pointers to one object see each other's writes. The -> operator reaches a member through a pointer, and const can protect either the pointer or the value it points at.

cards.q: int x{ 3 }; int* p{ &x }; *p = *p * 2; What is x?
What is the difference between p->hp and *p.hp?
cards.a: p->hp means (*p).hp, the member of the struct p points at. *p.hp tries to take member hp of the pointer and then dereference it, which does not compile for a plain pointer.

cards.q: Which of these compile? const int* a; *a = 1; and int* const b{ &x }; *b = 1;
cards.a: Only the second. a points at a const int so cannot write through it; b is a const pointer but the int it points at can change.

cards.q: Two pointers p and q hold the same address. *p = 9; What is *q?
